title: The churches — one Lord, many traditions, calibrated
body: Every major tradition of the Church, gathered from its own confession and measured against the one plumb-line: Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds. We calibrate, we do not judge — each tradition has kept a seed well; we name the gift and the ground held in common (Ephesians 4:4-6: one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith).

title: The ecumenical creeds — the shared ground
body: The ecumenical creeds — the shared ground. Confession: Apostles' Creed; Nicene Creed (325/381); Chalcedon (451). Central emphasis: the Trinity, the incarnation, the death and resurrection of Christ, the one holy catholic Church. The seed it has kept: the core every tradition below confesses together — the center that holds. Anchored on: Matthew 28:19; 1 Corinthians 15:3-4; John 1:1-14. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Eastern Orthodoxy
body: Eastern Orthodoxy. Confession: the Nicene Creed (without the filioque); the Seven Ecumenical Councils. Central emphasis: the unbroken worship and doctrine of the ancient Church; theosis — union with God; the mystery of the liturgy. The seed it has kept: continuity with the undivided Church and a deep reverence before the mystery of God. Anchored on: John 17:21-23; 2 Peter 1:4; Psalm 46:10. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Lutheran

Central emphasis: justification by grace alone through faith alone; law and gospel rightly divided; the Word and the sacraments. The seed it has kept: the recovery of grace — that we are saved by Christ's work received, not our own achieved. Anchored on: Romans 3:28; Ephesians 2:8-9; Galatians 2:16. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Athanasius of Alexandria — The ecumenical creeds — the shared ground
body: Athanasius of Alexandria (c. 296-373) — the voice of the The ecumenical creeds — the shared ground tradition, by its own reckoning: the defender of Nicene faith when nearly the whole world wavered — 'Athanasius contra mundum'. The gift the whole church receives: that the Son is true God of true God — the confession every tradition below still shares. Honest on both ends: his fierceness in controversy was real; exiles were mutual and the era's polemics were harsh on all sides. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: 'He became what we are, that He might make us what He is' — the whole point is Christ (John 1:14). [public domain (On the Incarnation and the festal letters are freely available)]

title: John Chrysostom — Eastern Orthodoxy
body: John Chrysostom (c. 347-407) — the voice of the Eastern Orthodoxy tradition, by its own reckoning: the 'Golden-mouthed' preacher whose Divine Liturgy the Orthodox pray to this day. The gift the whole church receives: preaching that weds Scripture to the poor — 'if you cannot find Christ in the beggar at the church door, you will not find Him in the chalice'. Honest on both ends: his sermons against the Jews of Antioch are a real and grievous stain, named honestly by historians of every tradition. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: his last words: 'Glory be to God for all things' — a life preached toward Christ (Matthew 25:40). [public domain (homilies widely available)]

title: Thomas Aquinas — Roman Catholicism
body: Thomas Aquinas (1225-1274) — the voice of the Roman Catholicism tradition, by its own reckoning: the Angelic Doctor — the tradition's own summa of faith seeking understanding. The gift the whole church receives: the confidence that faith and reason are one gift from one God — grace perfects nature. Honest on both ends: his system is held authoritative by Rome in a way the wider church does not bind itself to; he himself called it 'straw' beside what he saw of Christ. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: at the end he left the Summa unfinished: 'I can write no more; all I have written seems like straw' — beside the Person he had met (Philippians 3:8). [public domain (the Summa is freely available)]

title: Martin Luther — Lutheran
body: Martin Luther (1483-1546) — the voice of the Lutheran tradition, by its own reckoning: the reformer the tradition bears the name of — the recovery of justification by faith. The gift the whole church receives: that the gospel is a gift received, not a wage earned — grace alone, through faith alone. Honest on both ends: his late writings against the Jews are indefensible and are repudiated by Lutheran bodies themselves — honesty requires saying so plainly. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: 'the cross alone is our theology' — everything he recovered points at Christ crucified (Romans 1:17). [public domain (the catechisms, commentaries and hymns are freely available)]

title: John Calvin — Reformed / Presbyterian
body: John Calvin (1509-1564) — the voice of the Reformed / Presbyterian tradition, by its own reckoning: the Institutes' author — the tradition's systematic voice of God's sovereignty. The gift the whole church receives: a God-centered vision of the whole of life, and rigorous submission of every claim to Scripture. Honest on both ends: the execution of Servetus in Geneva happened with his concurrence; Reformed historians name it without excuse. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: 'we are not our own; we are God's' — the sovereignty he preached was Christ's claim on the whole person (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). [public domain (the Institutes and commentaries are freely available)]

title: Thomas Cranmer — Anglican
body: Thomas Cranmer (1489-1556) — the voice of the Anglican tradition, by its own reckoning: the Prayer Book's author — the cadences Anglicans have prayed for five centuries. The gift the whole church receives: common prayer that catechizes a whole people — worship as formation. Honest on both ends: he recanted under threat and then recanted his recantation at the stake, thrusting the offending hand into the fire first — a flawed man whose end was honest. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: his collects gather every prayer 'through Jesus Christ our Lord' — the Book's constant resolution (Colossians 3:16). [public domain (the Book of Common Prayer 1549/1552/1662)]

title: Charles Spurgeon — Baptist
body: Charles Spurgeon (1834-1892) — the voice of the Baptist tradition, by its own reckoning: the 'Prince of Preachers' — the voice Baptists themselves hold highest. The gift the whole church receives: plain gospel preaching to ordinary people, and a pastor's heart for the poor and the orphan. Honest on both ends: he broke fellowship in the Downgrade Controversy — some judge the break prophetic, others needlessly sharp; both readings are carried. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: 'I take my text and make a beeline to the cross' — his own stated method (1 Corinthians 2:2). [public domain (thousands of sermons freely available — some already in this keeping)]

title: John Wesley — Methodist / Wesleyan
body: John Wesley (1703-1791) — the voice of the Methodist / Wesleyan tradition, by its own reckoning: the founder whose Standard Sermons the tradition made its doctrinal standard. The gift the whole church receives: grace offered to every person, and holiness pursued as the real shape of salvation — faith working by love. Honest on both ends: his marriage was unhappy and his organizational splits from Anglicanism were contested in his own lifetime — the tradition tells it honestly. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: 'the best of all is, God is with us' — his dying words, the whole method's resolution (Hebrews 12:14). [public domain (sermons and journals freely available)]

title: William J. Seymour — Pentecostal / Charismatic
body: William J. Seymour (1870-1922) — the voice of the Pentecostal / Charismatic tradition, by its own reckoning: the Azusa Street revival's pastor — the fountainhead the tradition itself names. The gift the whole church receives: the expectation that the Spirit still falls on all flesh — and a revival that crossed the color line when almost nothing else did. Honest on both ends: the movement he birthed fractured along the very racial lines Azusa had crossed; the tradition's own historians grieve it. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: he preached that the gifts exist to exalt Jesus, not the gifted — 'the baptism is to give you power to witness to Christ' (Acts 1:8). [public domain (The Apostolic Faith papers, 1906-1908)]

title: Menno Simons — Anabaptist
body: Menno Simons (1496-1561) — the voice of the Anabaptist tradition, by its own reckoning: the shepherd the Mennonites bear the name of — discipleship under persecution. The gift the whole church receives: that following Jesus is the substance of faith — peace, community, and a church that cannot coerce. Honest on both ends: his strict church discipline (the ban) divided families and is debated within the tradition itself. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: his motto, kept on every title page: 'No other foundation can any one lay than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ' (1 Corinthians 3:11). [public domain (the Foundation Book is freely available)]

title: Jonathan Edwards — Congregational / Free Church
body: Jonathan Edwards (1703-1758) — the voice of the Congregational / Free Church tradition, by its own reckoning: America's theologian — the congregational tradition's towering mind and revival preacher. The gift the whole church receives: the beauty and weight of God — religious affections tested by their fruit, not their heat. Honest on both ends: he owned slaves; the tradition that honors his theology says so plainly and does not look away. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: 'The redeemed have all their inherent good in Christ' — his sermons return there relentlessly (John 1:16). [public domain (the works are freely available)]

title: Ellen G. White — Seventh-day Adventist
body: Ellen G. White (1827-1915) — the voice of the Seventh-day Adventist tradition, by its own reckoning: the messenger the tradition itself names — her counsels shaped its mission, schools and hospitals. The gift the whole church receives: steadfastness on the Sabbath as gift, the soon return of Christ, and whole-person care for health. Honest on both ends: Adventists hold her writings as an inspired lesser light; the wider church does not — both positions are stated, neither is flattened. Her own rule is kept: the Bible is the greater light by which the lesser is tested. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: 'lift up Jesus, the Man of Calvary, higher and still higher' — her constant charge (John 12:32). [public domain (Steps to Christ, The Desire of Ages and more are freely available)]

title: Alexander Campbell — Restoration Movement (Churches of Christ / Disciples)
body: Alexander Campbell (1788-1866) — the voice of the Restoration Movement (Churches of Christ / Disciples) tradition, by its own reckoning: the Restoration's chief editor and debater — 'where the Scriptures speak, we speak'. The gift the whole church receives: the plea to be simply Christian — Scripture as the pattern and the unity of all believers as the aim. Honest on both ends: the movement devoted to unity itself divided over instruments and societies; its own historians name the irony. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: his plea's whole ground: the church rests on the one confession — 'Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God' (Matthew 16:16). [public domain (The Christian System is freely available)]

title: Billy Graham — Evangelical / Interdenominational
body: Billy Graham (1918-2018) — the voice of the Evangelical / Interdenominational tradition, by its own reckoning: the evangelist the whole movement names first — crusades that preached to more people than any voice before him. The gift the whole church receives: one simple message carried across every denominational line, with financial and personal integrity kept deliberately (the Modesto Manifesto). Honest on both ends: he later regretted political entanglements and said so himself; his recordings and books remain under copyright, so this card carries facts and a pointer, never his text. And the voice itself resolves to Christ: his one sermon, by his own account: 'the Bible says' — and the invitation to come to Christ (John 14:6). [NOT public domain (d. 2018) — no text reproduced; see the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association archives]
